_meta.notes: Decision Utility is a derived planning layer above verified claims. Seeds inform wording only. Any new legal proposition requires an independent claim path.

decision_objects.title: Territorial applicability
decision_objects.question: Which Article 3 limb(s), if any, map the intended European activity for this entry plan?
decision_objects.evidence: Inspect establishment reach (EP-CLM-000018), offering of goods or services (EP-CLM-000019), and monitoring of behaviour (EP-CLM-000020). Art. 3(3) remains deferred/unminted in batch-1 and must not be invented here.
decision_objects.planning_consequence: Close the territorial map before freezing entity design, go-to-market packaging, or tracking/analytics architecture. EU establishment design, offering signals (language, shipping, pricing), and monitoring design are entry gates - not post-launch cleanup.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Whether a concrete establishment exists; whether a concrete offering targets data subjects in the Union; whether a concrete monitoring design observes behaviour in the Union; any Art. 3(3) analysis.
hard_rules: Do not declare that a named unknown company is in or out of GDPR scope.
Do not collapse the three limbs into one slogan.

decision_objects.title: Operating role
decision_objects.question: For each material processing activity, who determines purposes and means, who processes on behalf of whom, and where are joint-controller arrangements required?
decision_objects.evidence: Controller definition (EP-CLM-000021), processor definition (EP-CLM-000022), and joint-controller arrangement duty (EP-CLM-000023).
decision_objects.planning_consequence: Close the role map before contracting, sub-processor graphs, transfer tools, or marketplace partnership launch. Vendor classification and responsibility allocation are pre-entry gates.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Actual purpose/means determination on each activity; contractual reality versus labels; whether two or more actors jointly determine purposes and means.
hard_rules: Do not equate vendor labels with legal role.
Do not treat joint-controller status as optional branding.

decision_objects.title: EU representative
decision_objects.question: If Article 3(2) applies to the activity, does the Art. 27(1) representative duty apply, or does an Art. 27(2) exception close the gate?
decision_objects.evidence: Default duty where Art. 3(2) applies (EP-CLM-000024) must be co-rendered with Art. 27(2) exceptions (EP-CLM-000025). Neither claim may be cited as a standalone conclusion.
decision_objects.planning_consequence: Representative status must be closed before freezing the European operating model. The gate cannot be closed without documenting the Art. 27(2) analysis alongside the Art. 27(1) default.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Whether Art. 3(2) actually applies; whether processing is occasional / large-scale special categories or Art. 10 data / unlikely to result in risk; whether the actor is a public authority or body.
hard_rules: Never say 'your company needs an EU representative' as a graph conclusion.

decision_objects.title: Lawfulness baseline
decision_objects.question: For each material processing activity, which Art. 6(1) basis is relied on, how do Art. 5(1) principles constrain the design, and what accountability evidence will demonstrate that map?
decision_objects.evidence: Lawfulness requires at least one Art. 6(1)(a)-(f) basis (EP-CLM-000026); Art. 5(1) principles (EP-CLM-000027); Art. 5(2) accountability (EP-CLM-000028).
decision_objects.planning_consequence: Build a legal-basis map and a governance evidence pack before EU launch. Product data model and retention design are constrained by the principles before market activation.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Which concrete basis applies to each activity; whether consent is actually used or appropriate; how purpose limitation, minimisation, and storage limitation bind a specific product; what records will demonstrate accountability.
hard_rules: Art. 6 is a structural gate - not a slogan that 'consent is required'.
Do not elevate one Art. 6(1) basis as the universal default.

decision_objects.title: Governance readiness
decision_objects.question: Is the operating model ready on Art. 24/25/28/30/32 before EU ops freeze - including RoPA with its Art. 30(5) qualification?
decision_objects.evidence: Controller responsibility (EP-CLM-000029), data protection by design/default (EP-CLM-000030), processor/sub-processor controls (EP-CLM-000031), records of processing (EP-CLM-000032) co-rendered with Art. 30(5) (EP-CLM-000033), and security appropriate to risk (EP-CLM-000034).
decision_objects.planning_consequence: Treat security/governance design, product architecture, vendor graph, and RoPA as pre-entry deliverables. Headcount alone does not close the RoPA gate; Art. 30(5) must be analysed with the Art. 30(1)-(2) default.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Risk profile of concrete processing; whether <250-person organisations meet any Art. 30(5) re-trigger (risk / not occasional / special categories or Art. 10); vendor diligence outcomes; chosen technical and organisational measures.
hard_rules: Never present Art. 30 as an automatic exemption for organisations under 250 persons.

decision_objects.title: Breach response
decision_objects.question: Does the incident path distinguish supervisory-authority notification (Art. 33) from data-subject communication (Art. 34), including each default and its qualification?
decision_objects.evidence: Art. 33(1) notify default (EP-CLM-000035) co-rendered with unlikely-to-result-in-risk qualifier (EP-CLM-000036); Art. 34(1)-(2) communicate default (EP-CLM-000037) co-rendered with Art. 34(3) exceptions (EP-CLM-000038).
decision_objects.planning_consequence: Incident-response design is a pre-entry operational gate. Playbooks must encode risk-threshold assessment and Art. 34(3) branches - not only a 72-hour timer - and must keep SA notify vs data-subject communicate as separate decisions.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Concrete breach facts; risk and high-risk assessments; whether a delay reason applies; whether any Art. 34(3) branch is met.
hard_rules: Never collapse Art. 33 and Art. 34 into one notice duty.
Never render either default without its qualifier pair.

decision_objects.title: DPIA / DPO triggers
decision_objects.question: Which features trigger a DPIA under Art. 35, and which Art. 37(1)(a)/(b)/(c) triggers, if any, require DPO designation?
decision_objects.evidence: DPIA high-risk gate and particular cases (EP-CLM-000039); DPO designation as Art. 37(1) trigger model (EP-CLM-000040).
decision_objects.planning_consequence: High-risk feature design must test DPIA before EU activation. Org design tests Art. 37(1) triggers and does not assume a default DPO for every operator.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Whether a concrete processing is likely to result in high risk; which particular cases apply; whether a public authority / core-activity large-scale special categories or monitoring trigger is met.
hard_rules: Art. 37 is a trigger model - not a universal DPO duty.
Do not invent Art. 9 special-category claims beyond verified batch-1 scope.

decision_objects.title: International transfer path
decision_objects.question: Before freezing cloud regions and vendors, what Chapter V path governs any transfer - following 44 -> 45 -> 46 -> 49 rather than treating those as equal options?
decision_objects.evidence: General transfer gate (EP-CLM-000041), then adequacy where a valid decision exists (EP-CLM-000042), then appropriate safeguards (EP-CLM-000043), then derogations (EP-CLM-000044). These are related pathway claims, not qualified_by pairs and not interchangeable options. Dynamic adequacy-country lists remain deferred/unminted.
decision_objects.planning_consequence: Design transfer architecture before freezing regions/vendors. Adequacy may be used only where a valid decision exists and must be re-checked under freshness rules. SCC/BCR/contract design precedes vendor freeze. Art. 49 must not be treated as the default transfer design.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Whether a concrete transfer occurs; destination; existence and validity of an adequacy decision at decision time; which Art. 46 tool is actually available; whether any Art. 49 derogation conditions are met.
hard_rules: Never present adequacy, SCC/BCR, and Art. 49 as equal menu options.
Never treat Art. 49 as the planned default path.

decision_objects.title: Enforcement exposure
decision_objects.question: How should board and risk framing present Art. 83 exposure - criteria and tiers rather than a single scare figure?
decision_objects.evidence: Administrative fines retain criteria plus tiers (EP-CLM-000045). Regulation (EU) 2025/2518 remains Freshness Watch only and is not a batch-1 claim.
decision_objects.planning_consequence: Risk register and board framing use the Art. 83 structure and criteria - not a single maximum figure detached from the statutory method.
decision_objects.what_remains_fact_specific: Concrete infringement facts; which tier/criteria apply; turnover or other calculation inputs; any future instrument effect under freshness watch.
hard_rules: Do not reduce Art. 83 to a scare headline number.
Do not mint 2025/2518 as a verified claim inside R2.6.
